audit_status.source_base: Hebrew source via Sefaria with source/English versification reconciliation; public-domain KJV familiar comparison
audit_status.review_note: Draft follows Hebrew narrative; renders divine name as YHWH. Keeps moral difficulty and variant markers (Babylon/Babel). Requires witness-check versus 2 Kings and the Prayer of Manasseh tradition.

verses.restored: Manasseh was twelve years old when he began to reign; and he reigned fifty and five years in Jerusalem.

familiar.text: Manasseh was twelve years old when he began to reign, and he reigned fifty and five years in Jerusalem:

modern.text: Manasseh was twelve years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem fifty-five years.

original.text: בֶּן שְׁתֵּ֥ים עֶשְׂרֵ֛ה שָׁנָ֖ה מְנַשֶּׁ֣ה בְמָלְכ֑וֹ וַחֲמִשִּׁ֤ים וְחָמֵשׁ֙ שָׁנָ֔ה מָלַ֖ךְ בִּירוּשָׁלִָֽם

verses.restored: But he did that which was evil in the sight of YHWH, like the abominations of the nations whom YHWH had cast out before the people of Israel.

familiar.text: But did that which was evil in the sight of the LORD, like unto the abominations of the heathen, whom the LORD had cast out before the children of Israel.

notes.title: short
notes.body: Language echoes covenantal warning against foreign cults.

modern.text: And he did evil in the sight of the LORD by following the abominations of the nations that the LORD had driven out before the Israelites.

original.text: וַיַּ֥עַשׂ הָרַ֖ע בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה כְּתֽוֹעֲבוֹת֙ הַגּוֹיִ֔ם אֲשֶׁר֙ הוֹרִ֣ישׁ יְהוָ֔ה מִפְּנֵ֖י בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל

verses.restored: He rebuilt the high places which Hezekiah his father had broken down; he reared up altars for Baʿalim, made Asherim, worshipped all the host of heaven, and served them.

familiar.text: For he built again the high places which Hezekiah his father had broken down, and he reared up altars for Baalim, and made groves, and worshipped all the host of heaven, and served them.

notes.title: short
notes.body: 'Host of heaven' implies astral cultic worship; Asherim = cultic poles/groves.

modern.text: For he rebuilt the high places that his father Hezekiah had torn down, and he raised up altars for the Baals and made Asherah poles. And he worshiped and served all the host of heaven.

original.text: וַיָּ֗שָׁב וַיִּ֨בֶן֙ אֶת הַבָּמ֔וֹת אֲשֶׁ֥ר נִתַּ֖ץ יְחִזְקִיָּ֣הוּ אָבִ֑יו וַיָּ֨קֶם מִזְבְּח֤וֹת לַבְּעָלִים֙ וַיַּ֣עַשׂ אֲשֵׁר֔וֹת וַיִּשְׁתַּ֨חוּ֙ לְכָל צְבָ֣א הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם וַֽיַּעֲבֹ֖ד אֹתָֽם

verses.restored: Also he built altars in the house of YHWH, whereof YHWH had said, 'In Jerusalem shall my name be for ever.'

familiar.text: Also he built altars in the house of the LORD, whereof the LORD had said, In Jerusalem shall my name be for ever.

modern.text: Manasseh also built altars in the house of the LORD, of which the LORD had said, “My Name will remain in Jerusalem forever.”

original.text: וּבָנָ֥ה מִזְבְּח֖וֹת בְּבֵ֣ית יְהוָ֑ה אֲשֶׁר֙ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה בִּירוּשָׁלִַ֥ם יִֽהְיֶה שְּׁמִ֖י לְעוֹלָֽם

verses.restored: And he built altars for all the host of heaven in the two courts of the house of YHWH.

familiar.text: And he built altars for all the host of heaven in the two courts of the house of the LORD.

modern.text: In both courtyards of the house of the LORD, he built altars to all the host of heaven.

original.text: וַיִּ֥בֶן מִזְבְּח֖וֹת לְכָל צְבָ֣א הַשָּׁמָ֑יִם בִּשְׁתֵּ֖י חַצְר֥וֹת בֵּית יְהוָֽה

verses.restored: And he caused his sons to pass through the fire in the Valley of Ben‑Hinnom; and he observed times, used augury, witchcraft, consulted familiar spirits and wizards; he wrought much evil in the sight of YHWH, to provoke him to anger.

familiar.text: And he caused his children to pass through the fire in the valley of the son of Hinnom: also he observed times, and used enchantments, and used witchcraft, and dealt with a familiar spirit, and with wizards: he wrought much evil in the sight of the LORD, to provoke him to anger.

notes.title: short
notes.body: 'Pass through the fire' implies child sacrifice in the valley (Gei‑Ben‑Hinnom).

modern.text: He sacrificed his sons in the fire in the Valley of Hinnom. He practiced sorcery, divination, and witchcraft, and consulted mediums and spiritists. He did great evil in the sight of the LORD, provoking Him to anger.

original.text: וְהוּא֩ הֶעֱבִ֨יר אֶת בָּנָ֤יו בָּאֵשׁ֙ בְּגֵ֣י בֶן הִנֹּ֔ם וְעוֹנֵ֤ן וְנִחֵשׁ֙ וְֽכִשֵּׁ֔ף וְעָ֥שָׂה א֖וֹב וְיִדְּעוֹנִ֑י הִרְבָּ֗ה לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת הָרַ֛ע בְּעֵינֵ֥י יְהוָ֖ה לְהַכְעִיסֽוֹ

verses.restored: And he set the carved image, the idol which he had made, in the house of God; of which God had said to David and to Solomon his son, 'In this house, and in Jerusalem, which I have chosen out of all the tribes of Israel, will I put my name for ever.'

familiar.text: And he set a carved image, the idol which he had made, in the house of God, of which God had said to David and to Solomon his son, In this house, and in Jerusalem, which I have chosen before all the tribes of Israel, will I put my name for ever:

notes.title: short
notes.body: Quotation of YHWH's promise contrasts with the idol's installation.

modern.text: Manasseh even took the carved image he had made and set it up in the house of God, of which God had said to David and his son Solomon, “In this temple and in Jerusalem, which I have chosen out of all the tribes of Israel, I will establish My Name forever.

original.text: וַיָּ֕שֶׂם אֶת פֶּ֥סֶל הַסֶּ֖מֶל אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֑ה בְּבֵ֣ית הָאֱלֹהִ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֨ר אָמַ֤ר אֱלֹהִים֙ אֶל דָּוִיד֙ וְאֶל שְׁלֹמֹ֣ה בְנ֔וֹ בַּבַּ֨יִת הַזֶּ֜ה וּבִֽירוּשָׁלִַ֗ם אֲשֶׁ֤ר בָּחַ֨רְתִּי֙ מִכֹּל֙ שִׁבְטֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אָשִׂ֥ים אֶת שְׁמִ֖י לְעֵילֽוֹם

verses.restored: And I will not any more remove the foot of Israel from out of the land which I have appointed for your fathers—only if they will be careful to do all that I have commanded them, according to all the law, statutes, and ordinances by the hand of Moses.

familiar.text: Neither will I any more remove the foot of Israel from out of the land which I have appointed for your fathers; so that they will take heed to do all that I have commanded them, according to the whole law and the statutes and the ordinances by the hand of Moses.

modern.text: I will never again cause the feet of the Israelites to leave the land that I assigned to your fathers, if only they are careful to do all that I have commanded them through Moses—all the laws, statutes, and judgments.”

original.text: וְלֹ֣א אוֹסִ֗יף לְהָסִיר֙ אֶת רֶ֣גֶל יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל מֵעַל֙ הָֽאֲדָמָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר הֶֽעֱמַ֖דְתִּי לַאֲבֹֽתֵיכֶ֑ם רַ֣ק אִם יִשְׁמְר֣וּ לַעֲשׂ֗וֹת אֵ֚ת כָּל אֲשֶׁ֣ר צִוִּיתִ֔ים לְכָל הַתּוֹרָ֛ה וְהַֽחֻקִּ֥ים וְהַמִּשְׁפָּטִ֖ים בְּיַד מֹשֶֽׁה

verses.restored: So Manasseh led Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem to do worse than the nations whom YHWH had destroyed before the children of Israel.

familiar.text: So Manasseh made Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem to err, and to do worse than the heathen, whom the LORD had destroyed before the children of Israel.

modern.text: So Manasseh led the people of Judah and Jerusalem astray, so that they did greater evil than the nations that the LORD had destroyed before the Israelites. Manasseh’s Repentance and Restoration (2 Kings 21:10–18)

original.text: וַיֶּ֣תַע מְנַשֶּׁ֔ה אֶת יְהוּדָ֖ה וְיֹשְׁבֵ֣י יְרוּשָׁלִָ֑ם לַעֲשׂ֣וֹת רָ֔ע מִן הַ֨גּוֹיִ֔ם אֲשֶׁר֙ הִשְׁמִ֣יד יְהוָ֔ה מִפְּנֵ֖י בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל

verses.restored: And YHWH spoke to Manasseh and to his people, but they would not give ear.

familiar.text: And the LORD spake to Manasseh, and to his people: but they would not hearken.

modern.text: And the LORD spoke to Manasseh and his people, but they did not listen.

original.text: וַיְדַבֵּ֧ר יְהוָ֛ה אֶל מְנַשֶּׁ֥ה וְאֶל עַמּ֖וֹ וְלֹ֥א הִקְשִֽׁיבוּ

verses.restored: Therefore YHWH brought upon them the captains of the host of the king of Assyria; and they took Manasseh among the thorns, bound him with fetters, and carried him to Babel (Babylon).

familiar.text: Wherefore the LORD brought upon them the captains of the host of the king of Assyria, which took Manasseh among the thorns, and bound him with fetters, and carried him to Babylon.

notes.title: short
notes.body: Hebrew text reads 'Babel'—assess witness tradition for 'Babylon' rendering.

modern.text: So the LORD brought against them the military commanders of the king of Assyria, who captured Manasseh, put a hook in his nose, bound him with bronze shackles, and took him to Babylon.

original.text: וַיָּבֵ֨א יְהוָ֜ה עֲלֵיהֶ֗ם אֶת שָׂרֵ֤י הַצָּבָא֙ אֲשֶׁר֙ לְמֶ֣לֶךְ אַשּׁ֔וּר וַיִּלְכְּד֥וּ אֶת מְנַשֶּׁ֖ה בַּחֹחִ֑ים וַיַּֽאַסְרֻ֨הוּ֙ בַּֽנְחֻשְׁתַּ֔יִם וַיּוֹלִיכֻ֖הוּ בָּבֶֽלָה

verses.restored: And when he was in affliction he besought YHWH his God, and humbled himself greatly before the God of his fathers.

familiar.text: And when he was in affliction, he besought the LORD his God, and humbled himself greatly before the God of his fathers,

modern.text: And in his distress, Manasseh sought the favor of the LORD his God and earnestly humbled himself before the God of his fathers.

original.text: וּכְהָצֵ֣ר ל֔וֹ חִלָּ֕ה אֶת פְּנֵ֖י יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהָ֑יו וַיִּכָּנַ֣ע מְאֹ֔ד מִלִּפְנֵ֖י אֱלֹהֵ֥י אֲבֹתָֽיו

verses.restored: And he prayed unto him, and YHWH was entreated for him, and he brought him again to Jerusalem into his kingdom. Then Manasseh knew that YHWH was God.

familiar.text: And prayed unto him: and he was intreated of him, and heard his supplication, and brought him again to Jerusalem into his kingdom. Then Manasseh knew that the LORD he was God.

modern.text: And when he prayed to Him, the LORD received his plea and heard his petition; so He brought him back to Jerusalem and to his kingdom. Then Manasseh knew that the LORD is God.

original.text: וַיִּתְפַּלֵּ֣ל אֵלָ֗יו וַיֵּעָ֤תֶר לוֹ֙ וַיִּשְׁמַ֣ע תְּחִנָּת֔וֹ וַיְשִׁיבֵ֥הוּ יְרוּשָׁלִַ֖ם לְמַלְכוּת֑וֹ וַיֵּ֣דַע מְנַשֶּׁ֔ה כִּ֥י יְהוָ֖ה ה֥וּא הָֽאֱלֹהִֽים

verses.restored: After this he built an outer wall to the city of David, on the west side of Gihon in the valley, even to the entrance at the Fish Gate; he compassed Ophel, and raised it very much, and placed captains of war in all the fortified cities of Judah.

familiar.text: Now after this he built a wall without the city of David, on the west side of Gihon, in the valley, even to the entering in at the fish gate, and compassed about Ophel, and raised it up a very great height, and put captains of war in all the fenced cities of Judah.

modern.text: After this, Manasseh rebuilt the outer wall of the City of David from west of Gihon in the valley to the entrance of the Fish Gate, and he brought it around the hill of Ophel and heightened it considerably. He also stationed military commanders in all the fortified cities of Judah.

original.text: וְאַחֲרֵי כֵ֡ן בָּנָ֣ה חוֹמָ֣ה חִֽיצוֹנָ֣ה לְעִיר דָּוִ֡יד מַעְרָבָה֩ לְגִיח֨וֹן בַּנַּ֜חַל וְלָב֨וֹא בְשַׁ֤עַר הַדָּגִים֙ וְסָבַ֣ב לָעֹ֔פֶל וַיַּגְבִּיהֶ֖הָ מְאֹ֑ד וַיָּ֧שֶׂם שָֽׂרֵי חַ֛יִל בְּכָל הֶעָרִ֥ים הַבְּצֻר֖וֹת בִּיהוּדָֽה

verses.restored: And he took away the foreign gods and the idol out of the house of YHWH, and all the altars that he had built on the mount of the house of YHWH and in Jerusalem; and he cast them out of the city.

familiar.text: And he took away the strange gods, and the idol out of the house of the LORD, and all the altars that he had built in the mount of the house of the LORD, and in Jerusalem, and cast them out of the city.

modern.text: He removed the foreign gods and the idol from the house of the LORD, along with all the altars he had built on the temple mount and in Jerusalem, and he dumped them outside the city.

original.text: וַ֠יָּסַר אֶת אֱלֹהֵ֨י הַנֵּכָ֤ר וְאֶת הַסֶּ֨מֶל֙ מִבֵּ֣ית יְהוָ֔ה וְכָל הַֽמִּזְבְּח֗וֹת אֲשֶׁ֥ר בָּנָ֛ה בְּהַ֥ר בֵּית יְהוָ֖ה וּבִירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וַיַּשְׁלֵ֖ךְ ח֥וּצָה לָעִֽיר

verses.restored: And he repaired the altar of YHWH, and sacrificed thereon peace‑offerings and thank‑offerings; and commanded Judah to serve YHWH the God of Israel.

familiar.text: And he repaired the altar of the LORD, and sacrificed thereon peace offerings and thank offerings, and commanded Judah to serve the LORD God of Israel.

notes.title: short
notes.body: Peace offerings (shelamim) and thank‑offerings (todah) mark cult renewal.

modern.text: Then he restored the altar of the LORD and sacrificed peace offerings and thank offerings on it, and he told Judah to serve the LORD, the God of Israel.

original.text: ויכן אֶת מִזְבַּ֣ח יְהוָ֔ה וַיִּזְבַּ֣ח עָלָ֔יו זִבְחֵ֥י שְׁלָמִ֖ים וְתוֹדָ֑ה וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ לִֽיהוּדָ֔ה לַעֲב֕וֹד אֶת יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל

verses.restored: Nevertheless the people still sacrificed in the high places, yet unto YHWH their God only.

familiar.text: Nevertheless the people did sacrifice still in the high places, yet unto the LORD their God only.

modern.text: Nevertheless, the people still sacrificed at the high places, but only to the LORD their God.

original.text: אֲבָל֙ ע֣וֹד הָעָ֔ם זֹבְחִ֖ים בַּבָּמ֑וֹת רַ֖ק לַיהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵיהֶֽם

verses.restored: Now the rest of the acts of Manasseh, and his prayer unto his God, and the words of the seers that spoke to him in the name of YHWH the God of Israel, are written in the records of the kings of Israel.

familiar.text: Now the rest of the acts of Manasseh, and his prayer unto his God, and the words of the seers that spake to him in the name of the LORD God of Israel, behold, they are written in the book of the kings of Israel.

notes.title: short
notes.body: 'Seers' (chazim) and 'prayer' suggest additional source material now lost or separate.

modern.text: As for the rest of the acts of Manasseh, along with his prayer to his God and the words of the seers who spoke to him in the name of the LORD, the God of Israel, they are indeed written in the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel.

original.text: וְיֶ֨תֶר דִּבְרֵ֣י מְנַשֶּׁה֮ וּתְפִלָּת֣וֹ אֶל אֱלֹהָיו֒ וְדִבְרֵי֙ הַֽחֹזִ֔ים הַֽמְדַבְּרִ֣ים אֵלָ֔יו בְּשֵׁ֥ם יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל הִנָּ֕ם עַל דִּבְרֵ֖י מַלְכֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל

verses.restored: His prayer also, and how God was entreated of him, and all his sins and his trespass, and the places wherein he built high places and set up Asherim and graven images before he was humbled, behold they are written among the sayings of the seers.

familiar.text: His prayer also, and how God was intreated of him, and all his sins, and his trespass, and the places wherein he built high places, and set up groves and graven images, before he was humbled: behold, they are written among the sayings of the seers.

modern.text: His prayer and how God received his plea, as well as all his sin and unfaithfulness, and the sites where he built high places and set up Asherah poles and idols before he humbled himself, they are indeed written in the Records of the Seers.

original.text: וּתְפִלָּת֣וֹ וְהֵֽעָתֶר לוֹ֮ וְכָל חַטָּאת֣וֹ וּמַעְלוֹ֒ וְהַמְּקֹמ֗וֹת אֲשֶׁר֩ בָּנָ֨ה בָהֶ֤ם בָּמוֹת֙ וְהֶעֱמִיד֙ הָאֲשֵׁרִ֣ים וְהַפְּסִלִ֔ים לִפְנֵ֖י הִכָּנְע֑וֹ הִנָּ֣ם כְּתוּבִ֔ים עַ֖ל דִּבְרֵ֥י חוֹזָֽי

verses.restored: So Manasseh slept with his fathers, and they buried him in his house; and Amon his son reigned in his stead.

familiar.text: So Manasseh slept with his fathers, and they buried him in his own house: and Amon his son reigned in his stead.

modern.text: And Manasseh rested with his fathers and was buried at his palace. And his son Amon reigned in his place. Amon Reigns in Judah (2 Kings 21:19–26)

original.text: וַיִּשְׁכַּ֤ב מְנַשֶּׁה֙ עִם אֲבֹתָ֔יו וַֽיִּקְבְּרֻ֖הוּ בֵּית֑וֹ וַיִּמְלֹ֛ךְ אָמ֥וֹן בְּנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּֽיו

verses.restored: Amon was twenty and two years old when he began to reign, and he reigned two years in Jerusalem.

familiar.text: Amon was two and twenty years old when he began to reign, and reigned two years in Jerusalem.

modern.text: Amon was twenty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem two years.

original.text: בֶּן עֶשְׂרִ֧ים וּשְׁתַּ֛יִם שָׁנָ֖ה אָמ֣וֹן בְּמָלְכ֑וֹ וּשְׁתַּ֣יִם שָׁנִ֔ים מָלַ֖ךְ בִּֽירוּשָׁלִָֽם

verses.restored: And he did that which was evil in the sight of YHWH, like as his father Manasseh had done: for Amon sacrificed unto all the carved images which Manasseh his father had made, and served them.

familiar.text: But he did that which was evil in the sight of the LORD, as did Manasseh his father: for Amon sacrificed unto all the carved images which Manasseh his father had made, and served them;

modern.text: And he did evil in the sight of the LORD, as his father Manasseh had done. Amon served and sacrificed to all the idols that his father Manasseh had made,

original.text: וַיַּ֤עַשׂ הָרַע֙ בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשָׂ֖ה מְנַשֶּׁ֣ה אָבִ֑יו וּֽלְכָל הַפְּסִילִ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֤ר עָשָׂה֙ מְנַשֶּׁ֣ה אָבִ֔יו זִבַּ֥ח אָמ֖וֹן וַיַּֽעַבְדֵֽם

verses.restored: And he humbled not himself before YHWH, as Manasseh his father had humbled himself; but Amon trespassed more and more.

familiar.text: And humbled not himself before the LORD, as Manasseh his father had humbled himself; but Amon trespassed more and more.

modern.text: but he did not humble himself before the LORD as his father Manasseh had done; instead, Amon increased his guilt.

original.text: וְלֹ֤א נִכְנַע֙ מִלִּפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה כְּהִכָּנַ֖ע מְנַשֶּׁ֣ה אָבִ֑יו כִּ֛י ה֥וּא אָמ֖וֹן הִרְבָּ֥ה אַשְׁמָֽה

verses.restored: And his servants conspired against him, and slew him in his own house.

familiar.text: And his servants conspired against him, and slew him in his own house.

modern.text: Then the servants of Amon conspired against him and killed him in his palace.

original.text: וַיִּקְשְׁר֤וּ עָלָיו֙ עֲבָדָ֔יו וַיְמִיתֻ֖הוּ בְּבֵיתֽוֹ

verses.restored: But the people of the land slew all them that had conspired against King Amon; and the people of the land made Josiah his son king in his stead.

familiar.text: But the people of the land slew all them that had conspired against king Amon; and the people of the land made Josiah his son king in his stead.

modern.text: But the people of the land killed all those who had conspired against King Amon, and they made his son Josiah king in his place.

translation_notes: Divine name יהוה rendered as YHWH throughout.
Preserves cultic terms (bamah, Asherah) and place-names (Gihon, Ophel, Babel) as transliterations where appropriate.
Does not harmonize Manasseh's repentance—reports both apostasy and restoration as in the Hebrew narrative.
safety_note: Contains unvarnished descriptions of child sacrifice, idolatry, political violence; intended for scholarly/faithful use, not for propagandistic or abusive ends.
